chunks: And you are not a guide to the blind against their misguidance; you make hear only those who believe in Our signs, so they are Muslims (submitting).

key_terms.آيَاتِنَا: Our signs (verses of the Quran or divine proofs)
key_terms.الْعُمْيِ: The blind (metaphor for those lacking spiritual insight)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet guiding and making people hear in Surah An-Naml?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies the distinction between the Prophet's duty to convey (tabligh) and God's exclusive power to guide (hidayah), emphasizing that effective reception requires internal receptivity. It underscores that 'making hear' is conditional upon the listener's willingness to submit (islam), linking the auditory experience of the message with the spiritual state of the believer. This reinforces the concept that guidance is a divine grace bestowed upon those who actively believe in the signs (ayat).
